title: Primary or secondary? It is about when, not how old

title: Primary or secondary? It is about when, not how old
node: AC9HH7S02 n1
summary: "A primary source comes from the time of the event you are investigating. A secondary source was made later, by someone looking back. The test is the time of the event, not how old the source is: a very old book written long after an event is still secondary, and something made last week can be primary for an event last week. Getting this right matters because every later question about a source depends on knowing which kind it is."
language: maths
hook: "Sima Qian's history of China is over two thousand years old. Is it a primary source about the Qin? It feels like it should be. Let's check."
---
Historians sort sources into two kinds, and the sorting depends on the question they are asking.

A **primary source** comes from the time of the event you are investigating. It was made then, by people who were there or had to deal with it. A **secondary source** was made later, by someone looking back at the event.

The test is not how old the source is. The test is: **was it made at the time of the event?**

## Predict: which is primary?

```step
stage: predict
insight: "Committing to an answer shows whether students sort by age or by time of the event."
check:
  type: predict
  q: "You are investigating how the First Emperor of Qin ruled, around 220 BCE. A history book written about 100 years later describes his rule. Is it primary or secondary?"
  options: ["Secondary: it was written 100 years later", "Primary: it is over 2000 years old", "Primary: it is a history of his rule", "Secondary: it is only one writer's view"]
  actual: "Secondary. It was written about a hundred years after the events, by someone looking back. Being very old does not make a source primary, being about his rule does not either, and one writer's view is not the test."
```

## Try: sort these sources

```step
stage: run
insight: "Sorting with the question 'was it made at the time?' makes the test usable, and the old-but-late source is the trap."
check:
  type: sort
  q: "You are investigating the First Emperor's rule (about 221 to 210 BCE). Is each source primary or secondary?"
  options: ["Primary", "Secondary"]
  items:
    - ["A law written on bamboo slips and buried with a Qin official in 217 BCE", "Primary", "It was made at the time, by someone living under those laws."]
    - ["One of the clay warriors made for the emperor's tomb", "Primary", "It was made during his reign, for him."]
    - ["A history of the Qin written about 100 years later by a Han court historian", "Secondary", "He was looking back on events he did not see."]
    - ["A museum label written in 2019 about the clay warriors", "Secondary", "It was written long after, by someone explaining them."]
    - ["A history of China printed 300 years ago", "Secondary", "It is old, but it was still written long after the Qin."]
```

Was your guess right? Notice the book printed 300 years ago. It is old, but old is not the test. It was still made long after the event, so it is secondary.

## Worked example: how old it is does not decide

```step
stage: investigate
insight: "Nib sorts by age. Watching the same reasoning fail on a source from a different event shows that the test is the time of the event."
tasks:
  - check:
      type: question
      q: "A student keeps a diary on the day of the school fair last term. She is investigating that fair. Is the diary primary or secondary?"
      options: ["Primary: it was written on the day of the event", "Secondary: a diary is one person's view, not the facts", "Secondary: it is only a few months old", "Primary, but only once it is many years old"]
      answer: 0
      feedback: [null, "Being one person's view does not make it secondary. What matters is that it was written at the time.", "How old a source is does not decide it. The time of the event does.", "It is primary now. Age does not change whether it was made at the time."]
      explain: "Primary. It was made on the day of the event by someone there. A recent source can be primary when the event is recent."
  - check:
      type: bug
      code: "working.txt#nib"
      text: "Nib is sorting a source for the First Emperor's rule. Click the first line where Nib's thinking goes wrong."
      answer: 4
      fault: logic
      misconception: old-means-primary
      explain: "Line 4: Nib thinks a source is primary because it is old. Sima Qian wrote about a hundred years after the Qin. Old is not the test. It was made long after the events, so it is secondary."
    smaller:
      check: { type: question, q: "Sima Qian wrote his history about 100 years after the Qin rulers. Was he alive when the First Emperor ruled?", options: ["No, so he was looking back", "Yes, he saw it happen", "Yes, because his book is over 2000 years old", "No, but his book is old, so it is still primary"], answer: 0, feedback: [null, "He wrote about 100 years later, so he could not have seen it.", "How old the book is does not tell you whether he was there.", "That is Nib's mistake. He was not there, so his book is secondary for the Qin."], explain: "He was not there. He wrote about events that happened before he was born." }
  - check:
      type: question
      q: "Which question best tells you whether a source is primary or secondary?"
      options: ["Was it made at the time of the event I am investigating?", "Is it more than a few hundred years old?", "Was it written by someone famous?", "Can I trust what it says?"]
      answer: 0
      feedback: [null, "Old is a trap. A very old source can still be secondary.", "Who wrote it does not decide when it was made compared with the event.", "Trust and primary are different things. A primary source can be wrong, and a secondary source can be right."]

```

### Same test, new source

The school fair diary was written on the day, so it is primary for the fair. Now think about a source that **changes** with the question. A museum label written in 2019 about the clay warriors is secondary if you are investigating the First Emperor: it was written over 2000 years later. But if you are investigating how museums explained the warriors in 2019, the same label was made at the time, so it is primary. The question you ask decides which kind of source it is.

## Vary: more sources

```step
stage: modify
insight: "Changing the event changes the answer, so the same source can be primary for one question and secondary for another."
tasks:
  - check:
      type: sort
      q: "You are investigating the school fair last term. Is each source primary or secondary?"
      options: ["Primary", "Secondary"]
      items:
        - ["A photo taken at the fair on the day", "Primary", "It was made at the time."]
        - ["A poster put up before the fair, advertising it", "Primary", "It was made at the time of the event, by the people running it."]
        - ["A newsletter article written the next term about the fair", "Secondary", "It was written after the fair, by someone looking back."]
        - ["A book about school fairs in general", "Secondary", "It was written later, and not about this fair."]
  - check:
      type: question
      q: "A 2019 museum label says the clay warriors were made for the First Emperor's tomb. You are investigating the museum's 2019 exhibition. Is the label primary or secondary?"
      options: ["Primary: it was made at the time of the exhibition", "Secondary: it is about the Qin, who lived long before", "Secondary: museum staff were explaining things, not taking part", "Primary: modern sources are always primary"]
      answer: 0
      feedback: [null, "Careful. What matters is which event you are investigating, not what the label talks about.", "Writing the label was part of the exhibition, so for this question the staff were taking part.", "Modern is not the test. A modern label is secondary for the Qin."]
      explain: "For the 2019 exhibition, the label is primary. For the Qin emperor's rule, the same label is secondary. The event you investigate decides."
```

## Practise: sort and explain

```step
stage: practise
insight: "Repeating the test on new sources so asking 'when was it made?' becomes the first move."
tasks:
  - check:
      type: sort
      q: "You are investigating how Qin officials kept law and order. Is each source primary or secondary?"
      options: ["Primary", "Secondary"]
      items:
        - ["Qin laws on bamboo slips found in an official's tomb", "Primary", "Made at the time, by and for officials."]
        - ["A textbook chapter on the Qin", "Secondary", "Written long after, to teach students."]
        - ["A Qin official's note about a case he judged", "Primary", "Made at the time by someone doing the job."]
        - ["A film about the First Emperor", "Secondary", "Made long after, by people retelling the story."]
  - check:
      type: question
      q: "Ravi says: 'This book is 400 years old, so it must be a primary source about the Qin.' What is the best reply?"
      options: ["It is old, but it was written long after the Qin, so it is secondary", "You are right: anything that old counts as primary", "No: books are always secondary, whenever they were written", "It is primary only if it quotes Qin sources"]
      answer: 0
      feedback: [null, "Check when the Qin were. A book 400 years old is still far later.", "Books can be primary, such as a diary written at the time. The time it was written decides.", "Quoting a Qin source does not make the book itself from the time. The quoted source is primary; the book is not."]
      explain: "Old is not the test. The Qin ruled over 2000 years ago, so a 400-year-old book is still a later retelling."
```

## Make: your own examples

```step
stage: make
insight: "Choosing sources about an event from your own life is how the test becomes yours."
check: { type: reflect, text: "In my own book I chose an event from my own life or school. I wrote one primary source and one secondary source for it, and a reason for each. A partner read it and gave feedback." }
```

Write it in your own book or document, not on this page. Your partner or teacher reads it.

## Typical: a tricky copy

```step
stage: make
tier: typical
insight: "A copy or translation of a primary source is an edge case: the content comes from the time, but the copy was made later."
check:
  type: question
  q: "A museum prints a photograph of one of the Qin bamboo slips. Which is the best way to think about it?"
  options: ["The slip is primary; the photo is a later copy of it", "The photo is new, so now the slip counts as secondary too", "The photo is primary for the Qin, because photos show things exactly", "The photo is useless, because only the real slip can be a source"]
  answer: 0
  feedback: [null, "The slip itself was made at the time. A later copy does not change that.", "A photo is not primary for the Qin just because it is a photo. It is a later copy of something that is.", "Photos can be useful. A copy of a source still carries what it shows."]
  explain: "The slip is the primary source. The photo shows it, so it is useful, but it was made later: use it carefully and check the slip if you can. Historians say which one they used."
```

## Wider: the same object both ways

```step
stage: make
tier: wider
insight: "One object can be primary for one question and secondary for another."
check: { type: reflect, text: "I found a source that is primary for one question and secondary for another, and explained why with a partner." }
```

Typical and wider steps are extras on the same idea. You do not need them to finish the lesson.

```teacher
learning: decide whether a source is primary or secondary for the event being
  investigated
summary: "Students learn that a source is primary if it was made at the time of
  the event being investigated, and secondary if it was made later by someone
  looking back. The test is the time of the event, not age. It is an optional
  catch-up for classes that need the idea: later lessons use the words primary
  and secondary, and students who sort by age will misread what a source can
  tell them."
time: 35
timing: Predict and Try 8 min · Worked example 10 min · Vary 7 min · Practise 5
  min · Make 5 min. Typical and wider steps are extras and not counted in this.
goals:
  - I can say whether a source is primary or secondary for a given event, and
    give a reason.
  - I can explain why a very old source can still be secondary.
  - I can name a primary and a secondary source for an event from my own life.
struggle: "Students sort by age: old means primary, new means secondary. The
  sort in Try puts a 300-year-old book on the secondary side on purpose. Let
  them argue it out before you say why."
before: >
  This is an optional warm-up, for classes that need the idea. It is tagged to
  the History skill AC9HH7S02 (locate primary and secondary sources), node 1,
  because the later lessons in this course use the words. A class that already
  sorts sources by the time of the event can skip it. It is listed as Optional,
  so it does not count towards finishing the course.


  The worked example uses ancient China in the Qin and Han period. It is a
  model: swap in the sources from your own depth study (Egypt, Greece, Rome,
  India or another) by keeping the question the same, was it made at the time of
  the event? Every source here is described in plain words, so nothing needs
  teaching first. Nothing is quoted from a published translation. The bamboo
  slips are real: a Qin official's tomb at Shuihudi was found with them in 1975.
  Sima Qian's history was written about a century after the Qin fell.


  The school fair examples, Nib and Ravi are made up. Do not ask students what
  their families did or have. The Make step asks for an event from their own
  life or school, but only what they choose to write, in their own book.
running:
  - "Predict: ask for a show of hands before the answer. The 100-years-later
    history is a good place to hear 'but it's really old'."
  - "Try: stop at the 300-year-old book and ask for a reason, not an answer."
  - "Worked example: let Nib's mistake sit before explaining it. Ask students
    which line is wrong, then why."
  - "Vary: the museum label is primary for one question and secondary for
    another. Ask students to say which question changed the answer."
  - "Make: read one or two out if students are happy to, without names."
stuck:
  - see: A student says a source is primary because it is old.
    ask: Was it made at the time of the event we are asking about?
    fix: Go back to the Sima Qian line. He wrote about a hundred years after the
      Qin. Old is not the test.
  - see: A student says secondary sources are worse than primary ones.
    ask: Worse for what question?
    fix: Neither kind is better. They are different. A secondary source can be
      right, and a primary source can be wrong.
  - see: A student says a recent source cannot be primary.
    ask: What if we are investigating something that happened last month?
    fix: Use the school fair diary. A recent source is primary for a recent event.
stretch: The same label or photo can be primary for one question and secondary
  for another. Find your own example and explain what changed. This is the same
  idea at greater width. It does not go on to the next lesson.
support: "A card with one question: 'Was it made at the time of the event I am
  asking about?' Students ask it of each source before sorting."
leads: >
  Next in Source origin and purpose: Who made it, and what does it show? (origin
  and content).


  Wider (teacher choice, not part of the student steps): ACARA's elaborations
  for AC9HH7S02 suggest categories for sorting sources, "such as scrolls, coins,
  artwork, human remains, primary perspectives and/or historical
  interpretations". Human remains are not used in this course's examples. If
  your unit includes them, follow your school's protocols and, for First Nations
  ancestral remains, local community guidance.
exit:
  q: What is the test for whether a source is primary or secondary, and why is it
    not how old it is?
  a: Whether it was made at the time of the event being investigated. An old
    source written long after the event is still secondary.
explain: >
  A **primary source** was made at the time of the event you are investigating.
  A **secondary source** was made later, by someone looking back.


  The test is the time of the event, not how old the source is. A source can be
  primary for one question and secondary for another.
class:
  inquiry:
    q: Two students are investigating the same school fair. One uses a photo taken
      on the day. The other uses an article written a year later. Whose source
      is better?
    prompts:
      - Better for what question?
      - What would the article writer know that the photo cannot show?
    notes: Steer away from 'primary is better'. The point is that they are different
      kinds, made at different times, for different questions.
  activities:
    - at: predict
      kind: activity
      title: Time line
      minutes: 4
      do: >
        Mark one end of the room Made at the time and the other Made later. Read
        out sources for the First Emperor's rule (a bamboo slip of laws, a clay
        warrior, a history written 100 years later, a museum label) and have
        students stand where they think each belongs. Ask a student in the
        middle for a reason.
      notes: Students in the middle have usually spotted the trap. Do not settle it.
        Ask for the reason.
    - at: make
      kind: discussion
      title: Your own event
      minutes: 4
      do: >
        Ask pairs to name one primary and one secondary source for an event at
        school. Collect a few and ask what they have in common.
      notes: They should all be about time, not age. If someone says 'old', ask what
        the event was.
  questions:
    - at: investigate
      title: Which is secondary?
      type: question
      q: Which of these is a secondary source about the First Emperor's rule?
      options:
        - A history written 100 years later
        - A law on a bamboo slip from his time
        - A clay warrior from his tomb
        - A stone inscription he ordered
      answer: 0
      explain: A history written a century later was made by someone looking back, so
        it is secondary.
```
